VendorcumProprie  COMPLAINT U/S 16 OF THE PREVENTION OF FOOD   ADULTERATION ACT, 1954  Serial number of the case : 209/03 Date of the commission of the offence : 10.07.2002 Date of filing of the complaint : 24.04.2003 CC No. 209/03 FI Vs. Suresh Bansal   Name of the Complainant, if any : Shri Suniti Kumar Gupta, F  Inspector Offence complained of or proved : Violation of provisions of S  2 (ia) (h) (j) & (m) of PF  1954; punishable U/s 1  r/w Section 7 of PFA Act  Plea of the accused : Pleaded not guilty Final order : Acquitted Arguments heard on : 12.03.2013 Judgment announced on : 20.03.2013 J U D G M E N T 1.

The present complaint has been filed on 24.04.2003 by the Delhi Administration through FI Sh.
Suniti Kumar Gupta against the accused Sh. Suresh Bansal.

It is stated in the complaint that on 10.07.2002 at about 4.30 PM, FI Sh. Suniti Kumar Gupta purchased a sample of Rai Whole, a food article for analysis from Sh. Suresh Bansal S/o late Sh. Sunder Lal Bansal at M/s Bansal Corner, C 3/1, Yamuna Vihar, Delhi53, who was found conducting the business of the said food article at the Fi vs .

Suresh Bansal Page 1 Of 13 on 20 March, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88656254/
1 time of sampling.

FI Sh. Suniti Kumar Gupta purchased approximately 600 gms. of Rai Whole,
taken from a jar closed with lid.
The sample was taken after mixing the Rai Whole with the help of a clean and dry Jhaba.

Thereafter, the sample was divided into three equal parts by putting it in three clean and dry bottles and each bottle containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to the PFA Act and Rules.
The signatures of vendor were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the bottles containing the sample.
Notice was given to accused and price of sample was also paid to the accused vide vendor receipt dated 10.07.2002.
Panchnama was also prepared at the spot.
All these documents prepared by FI Sh. Suniti Kumar Gupta were signed by accused Sh. Suresh Bansal, the vendor and the other witness namely Ms. Usha Kiran, FI.
It is stated that before starting sample proceedings, efforts were made to get the public witnesses to join the proceedings, but none came forward and as such Ms. Usha Kiran, FI joined as witness.

It is also stated that the sample was taken under the supervision of Sh. P.C. Jain, SDM/LHA.
2.
It is further stated that one counterpart of the sample in intact condition was sent to the Public Analyst, Delhi and two counterparts of the sample in intact conditions were deposited with LHA.
The Public Analyst analysed the sample and opined that "the sample is adulterated because it contains unpermitted oil soluble colouring matter".

It is further stated that Sh. Suresh Bansal was the VendorcumProprietor of M/s Bansal Corner and he being the incharge of the shop and was responsible for the day to day conduct of the business of the said shop.

Thereafter, the entire case file was sent to the Director, PFA who accorded the requisite consent U/s 20 of the Act and consequent thereto the present complaint was filed for violation of provisions of section 2 ((ia) (h),
(j) & (m) of the PFA Act, 1954 which is punishable U/s 16 (1) (A) r/w Section 7 of the said Act.
3. The accused was summoned vide order dated 24.04.2003.
The accused appeared and moved an application U/s 13 (2) of the Act to get analyzed the second counterpart of the sample from Central Food Laboratory (CFL).
The said application was allowed and consequently second counterpart of the sample was sent to CFL, Pune for analysis.

Director, CFL on analysing the second counterpart of the sample in question opined vide his Certificate dated 18.06.2003 that "sample does not conform to the standards of Mustard (Rai, Sarson) as per PFA Rules 1955"
4. Charge for voilation of Section 2 (ia) (a) (b), (j) & (m) of the PFA Act and for violation of Rule 23 r/w Rule 28 & 29 of PFA Rules punishable U/s 16 (1A) r/w Section 7 of the said was framed against the accused vide order dated 14.09.2009 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

5. Thereafter, prosecution examined 4 witnesses namely FI Baljit Singh as PW1, FI Sh. Suniti Kumar Gupta as PW2, Sh. P.C. Jain as PW3 and FI Ms. Usha Kiran as PW4 and PE was closed vide order dated 07.07.2010.
6. Statement of accused U/s 313 Cr.P.C. was recorded on 05.10.2010 wherein accused claimed himself to be innocent and opted for to lead evidence in his defence.
7. The accused has examined Sh. S.N. Mahendru as DW1 in his defence and DE was closed vide order dated 10.05.2011.

2 8.
I have heard the Ld. Counsel for the parties and perused the record carefully.

9. Ld. Counsel for accused has argued that there is variations in the report of Public Analyst (PA)
and Central Food Laboratory (CFL) and it shows that sample was not properly mixed and homogenized.

He further argued that Public Analyst did not find any synthetic colour in the sample and the sample is found to be coloured with unpermitted oil soluble added colouring matter as per PA report, while Director, CLF found two synthetic colour in the sample and it shows that wrong method of detecting the colour in the sample was adopted.
He has further argued that unless the colour is identified, there is possibility that colours detected in the sample are the inherent colours of the sample of Rai Whole.
10. On the other hand, the Ld. SPP for complainant has argued that variation in the report of PA and Director, CFL is of no consequence.

He contended that as per report of Director, CFL, the sample does not conform to the standards of Mustard (Rai, Sarson) and the report of Director, CFL being conclusive and supersedes the report of Public Analyst, therefore the accused cannot be given benefit of variations in the reports of PA and CFL.
11.
All the witnesses examined by the prosecution have deposed more or less as per the averments made in the complaint.

PW1 FI Baljeet Singh has deposed in his examinationinchief that on 10.07.2002 he along with FI Ms. Usha Kiran under the supervisions and directions of SDM/LHA Sh.
P.C. Jain visited the premises of M/s Bansal Corner, C3/1, Yamuna Vihar, Delhi where accused was found conducting the business of food articles stored there for sale for human consumption including Rai Whole.

He has further deposed that he purchased 600 gms of Rai Whole from the accused taken from a jar closed with lid bearing no label declaration for analysis on payment of Rs.
13.20/ vide vendor's receipt Ex. PW1/A.

He further deposed that before taking the sample, the Rai Whole was properly homogenized with the help of clean and dry Jhaba by rotating it in all possible directions and thereafter he divided the purchased sample into three equal parts by putting them in three clean and dry glass bottles and all the three sample bottles were separately packed,
marked, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules.
12. PW1 has further deposed that he prepared notice PW1/B and panchnama Ex. PW1/C and copy of the notice was also received by the accused and all the above documents were read over and explained to the accused in Hindi and he signed the same.

He has also deposed that one counter part of the sample alongwith one copy of memo in Form VII in intact & sealed condition was sent to the PA on 11.07.2002 vide receipt Ex. PW1/D and remaining two counter parts of the sample in a sealed packet were deposited in intact condition with the LHA on 11.07.2002 vide receipt Ex. PW 1/E.
He has further deposed that PA report was received which is Ex. PW1/F according to which the sample does not conform to the standards.
He has also deposed that thereafter he was dismissed from the service and further action was taken by FI Suniti Kumar Gupta.

Sh. Suniti Kumar Gupta further investigated the matter and sent a letter Ex. PW2/A to the vendor and vide its reply Ex. PW2/B, it was found that accused Sh. Suresh Bansal is the sole proprietor of the said firm.

He has also proved the letter sent to STO Ward No. 75 as Ex. PW2/C from the reply of which it was found that no such firm is found registered with the Sales Tax and the Fi vs . Suresh Bansal Page 1 Of 13 on 20 March, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88656254/
3
letter
sent to DHO, Shahdara North Zone Ex. PW2/D from the reply of which it was found that no health license was issued to M/s Bansal Corner.

He has also proved the sanction given by the Director, PFA for initiating the present prosecution against the accused as Ex. PW2/E, complaint as Ex. PW2/F and intimation letter given to accused along with PA report as Ex. PW2/G.

14. PW3 P.C. Jain under whom supervision and directions, the sample proceedings were conducted and PW4 FI Usha Kiran who was made a witness at the time of conducting the sample proceedings have deposed on the similar lines as deposed by PW1 and PW2 in their examination inchief.
15. In the crossexamination PW1 stated that he does not know who made the bottles clean and when.
He admitted that Rai belongs to mustard family and of different colours.
He stated that he cannot say that if the colour of Rai Whole is due to the presence of colour cartins oil in its outer pericarp.
He further stated that he does not know whether Rai is coated with colour or not, it is treated with solvent.

He further stated that he does not know if when put in solvent, its inherent colour also gets leached out the solvent and then it is not possible to distinguish between inherent colour and added colour.
16. PW3 stated in his crossexamination that he does not know that Rai belongs to mustard family or of different colours.
He further stated that he does not know that Rai Whole are the pericrap that is the outer skin of the Rai Whole contains colur cartins.
He further stated that he does not know if the inherent colour of the Rai gets leached into the solvent when Rai is treated with solvent to detect the colour/coating, if any.
PW4 also stated in her crossexamination that she does not know that Rai Whole contains its own natural inherent colour.

17. From the aforesaid crossexamination of PWs, the defence of the accused seems to be that the sample of the Rai Whole contains its natural inherent colour and he has not added any colour in Rai Whole as also stated by him in his statement U/s 313 Cr.P.C.
18.

In the present case it is not in dispute that on 10.07.2002 at about 4.30 PM, accused was found conducting the business of Rai Whole, a food article at M/s Bansal Corner, C3/1, Yamuna Vihar,
Delhi - 53 where the said food article was found stored for sale and further that the FI Baljit Singh lifted a sample of Rai Whole for analysis from the accused.

The sample was sent to the Public Analyst (PA) for analysis and the Public Analyst (PA) vide his report dated 29.07.2002 found that sample does not conform to standard because it is coloured with unpermitted oil soluble added colouring matter.
The present prosecution has been launched against the accused on the basis of said PA's report dated 29.07.2002.
The report of PA has been exhibited and proved as Ex. PW1/F.

The accused exercised his right u/s 13 (2) of the PFA Act and consequently second counterpart of the sample selected by the accused was sent to the Central Food Laboratory (CFL), Pune for analyzing the sample and the report thereof in the form of Certificate of the Director, CFL, Pune dated 18.06.2003 was received.
Perusal of same shows that sample does not conform to the standards of Mustard (Rai, Sarson) as per PFA Rules 1955.

Fi vs . Suresh Bansal Page 1 Of 13 on 20 March, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88656254/
4 19.
It is to be noted that in PA's report Ex. PW1/F, Organic extraneous matter was found to be 0.56%, while it was found to be 0.13% as per report of Director, CFL.
Similarly, inorganic extraneous matter was found to be 0.48% as per PA's report Ex. PW1/F, while it was 0.80% as per report of Director, CFL.
Further, as per report of PA Ex. PW1/F, edible oil seed of any other variety was found to be 0.03%, while it was nil as per report of Director, CFL.

It is also to be noted that PA vide his report Ex. PW1/F did not find any synthetic colour in the sample and only unpermitted oil soluble added colour was found, while Director, CFL detected two synthetic oil soluble colours in the sample i.e. red and orange.

20. As such, it is evident that there is huge variations in almost all the contents of the sample and it shows that proper method of detecting the colour was not applied or that the sample was not properly mixed or homogenized before lifting it.

In the case of State Vs. Suresh Kumar & Anr. 2010 (2) FAC 204, the Food Inspector visited the business store of the accused and purchased a sample of 'Rai Whole' from an open container for the purpose of analysis.

entities.text: State Vs. Suresh Kumar & Anr. 2010 (2) FAC 204
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The sample was sent to the Public Analyst and Central Food Laboratory for analysis and there was variations in the reports of both the experts and it was held by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court that sample of the article was not properly homogenized which has resulted in variations in the report of two Analysts and accused was acquitted.

21. In the present case also, there is huge variations in the report of Public Analyst (PA) and Central Food Laboratory (CFL) as stated herein above and it goes to show that the sample was not properly mixed up and hence it cannot be said to be representative sample and further that sample was homogenized before lifting it.
Therefore, benefit of doubt is liable to be given to the accused.

22. Furthermore, in his statement U/s 313 Cr.P.C, the accused came with a defence that there was no colour in the Rai Whole and it contains its own natural inherent colour and he has not added the colour in Rai Whole.

In support of his contention, the accused has examined Sh. S.N. Mahendru as DW1 who is Retd. Chief Chemist from The Regional Laboratory, Ghaziabad and having 40 years experience in the field of Food Analysis.

DW1 deposed in his examinationinchief that under the DGHS Manual of Analysis, it is mandatory to identify the colour/colours to find out if the same contains any added synthetic colours and if the colour has not been identified, it is not possible to know whether the colour detected was inherent (natural) or added.

He has placed on record the extracts from the Manual of Methods of Analysis published by Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Govt. of India, New Delhi as Ex. DW1/1.

He has also placed on record his book titled as Food Safety, A Technological Analysis published by Tata McGrawHill Publishing Company Ltd. as Ex. DW1/B.
23.
In the book written by DW1 Sh. S.N. Mahendru, on the subject of Food Safety A TechnoLegal Analysis, it has been stated that all varieties of mustard seed contain natural colour pigment of their own.

These colour pigments are also oil soluble and when the mustard seeds are treated with a solvent to detect the presence of added colour then the natural colour pigments present in the seed also get leached out in the solvent and when subjected to TLC test, it shows the presence of colour.

It is further reported in order to find out whether the colour is inherent or synthetic or added, it is compared with the known colours and thereafter, to distinguish between the natural colour or added Fi vs .

Suresh Bansal Page 1 Of 13 on 20 March, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88656254/
5 colour, solvent is sprinkled over a filter paper or the chromotograph itself is kept in an oven.
The natural colours have tendency to disappear within 3 or 4 days while synthetic colours last longer.

The entire procedure of testing of Rai and colour of Rai is explained in the book of DW1 Sh. S.N.
Mahenduru published by TATA McGraw Hill Publishing Ltd. on the subject of Food Safety A TechnoLegal Analysis, extracts of which has been placed on record by him as Ex. DW1/B.
24.

In the present case, as discussed herein above the Public Analyst vide his report Ex. PW1/F did not find any synthetic colour in the sample and only unpermitted oil soluble added colour was found, while Director, CFL detected two synthetic oil soluble colours in the sample commodity of Rai Whole i.e. red and orange.

In view of the evidence of DW1, it cannot be said that the prosecution has successfully identified the colour in the sample commodity of Rai Whole, whether it was its natural colour or it was added colour.
Therefore also, the accused is entitled for benefit of doubt.
Hence, accused is acquitted from the charges leveled against him.
Bail bonds stands cancelled.
File be consigned to Record Room.
